description.narrative:
This Nigeria–Hungary project strengthens youth influence and access to mental health systems through capacity building, community engagement, and policy advocacy. Youth in both countries face rising mental health challenges driven by stigma, social exclusion, andlimited youth-responsive services. The project will train youth leaders using expert-facilitated and step-down modules adapted for schools, IDP camps, and sports spaces, who will then cascade knowledge and psychosocial support to marginalized youth. Structured virtual exchanges will enable cross-continental learning and co-creation of solutions, while youth-authored advocacy briefs and socialmedia campaigns will engage policymakers and stakeholders. The partnership leverages WAVA’s youth-led policy mobilisation and BAIS’s community-based inclusion models to strengthen youth-responsive, accountable mental health systems. The project will culminate into an inclusive sport-athon showcasing youth mental health action.
The project aims to strengthen equitable access to youth-responsive mental health systems in Nigeria and Hungary by positioning marginalized young people as leaders in awareness, peer support, and policy advocacy. We seek to build a structured pathway that links community-based engagement; including sports-informed peer learning, with institutional dialogue and youth-authored policy recommendations.
Our key objectives are to equip marginalized youth with practical mental health knowledge and facilitation skills; foster structured cross-country learning between Nigerian and Hungarian youth advocates; and generate evidence-informed advocacy outputs that address systemic barriers such as stigma, limited service access, and weak youth representation in decision-making spaces.
In the short term, we expect increased mental health literacy, stronger peer support networks, and improved youth confidence in engaging policymakers. In the longer term, the project aims to institutionalize youth participation in mental health discussions, strengthen accountability between youth networks and public institutions, and produce a replicable cooperation model for cross-continental youth-led mental health advocacy. By connecting grassroots action to policy engagement, the initiative lays the foundation for sustained collaboration and scalable impact beyond the grant period.

participating-org.narrative:
Women Advocates for Vaccine Access (WAVA) is a youth-led, women-driven civil society organisation advancing equitable Primary Health Care and resilient health systems in Nigeria and across Africa. We focus on strengthening access, accountability, and youth participation within health governance, particularly for young women, adolescents, children, and other underserved populations.
Our vision is a society where young people; especially those from marginalized communities, have equitable access to quality healthcare, actively shape public policy, and lead sustainable, systems-level change.
Our mission is to strengthen inclusive and responsive health systems by generating evidence, mobilising youth voices, supporting programme implementation, and advocating for policies that ensure equitable access to vaccines and essential health services, regardless of socio-economic status.
WAVA operates at community, national, and regional levels, engaging in policy advocacy, research, youth capacity strengthening, and multi-stakeholder collaboration.We work closely with civil society networks, government institutions, and international partners to influence decision-making processes and improve accountability within health governance systems.
Our core objectives are to:
Advance equitable access to vaccinesand primary healthcare for vulnerable and underserved populations. Strengthen meaningful youth participation and leadership in health governance and policy processes. Generate and apply evidence to inform policy reform and improve health system performance. Foster strategic partnerships that bridge local realities with regional and global health agendas. Our values are youth leadership, equity, inclusion, accountability, collaboration, and sustainability. We prioritise transparency in governance and uphold the dignity, safety, and agency of all young people we engage.
